chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Al-Abbas ibn Amir, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

And the mothers should suckle their children. He (peace be upon him) said: As long as the child is in the stage of breastfeeding, he is between the two parents with equal right. So when he is weaned, the father has more right to him than the mother. So when the father dies, the mother has more right to him than the agnates (relatives).

If the father finds someone to breastfeed him for four dirhams, and the mother says, 'I will not breastfeed him except for five dirhams,' then he has the right to take him from her. However, it is better for him and more gentle with the child if he leaves him with his mother.
ai.seo_question: What are the Shia jurisprudential rules for child custody after weaning and in the event of the father's death?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of *hadanah* (custody), prioritizing the mother's physical care during nursing and the father's legal authority post-weaning, reflecting the Shia juristic view of complementary parental roles. It further illustrates the application of *khayr* (preference/best interest) in family law, where the father retains the right to dismiss the mother for excessive demands but is encouraged to maintain stability for the child's welfare. This ruling underscores the balance between legal entitlement and practical compassion in Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Al Abbas Bin Aamir, from Dawood Bin Al Husayn,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘

[2:233] And the mothers should suckle their children, for as long as the child is in the breast-feeding. So he would be between the two parents with the equality. So when it weans, then for the father is more right with him than the mother. So when the father dies, so the mother is more rightful with him that the relatives.

So if the father finds one who would breast-feed it for four Dirhams, and the mother says, ‘No, I will breast-feed it, except for five Dirhams, so it would be up to him if he snatches it from her, except if that is better for it, and she is more kind with it, if he were to leave it with its mother’.
en.sarwar: 4. Abu Ali al-Ash‘ariy has narrated from al-FIassan ibn Ali from al-‘Abbas ibn ‘Amir from Dawud ibn al-Hasin who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

Mothers must breastfeed their children’ means that a child during breastfeeding period is between the two parents in equal manners. When the child is weaned then the father has more right about him than the mother. When the father dies then the mother has more right than the relatives.

If the father finds a breastfeeding woman who asks four dirham, for example, and the mother says that she will not do for less than five dirham, he can take the child away from her unless she is more kind and better for the child.’”
